description: Issue #839 AC2, the cross-kind collision in the STRUCT-FIRST direction: `struct tally [ x y ]` then `define tally`. Its mirror (`define` then `struct`) is `struct-reserved-word-procedure`. Having both directions is what makes the pair meaningful: an implementation that only checked a `struct` name against already-declared procedures — but not a `define` name against already-declared structs — would report the mirror and be silent here, so this fixture is the one that fails for it. `spec/error-model.md:126` covers exactly this case: "a procedure and a struct with the same name in either order". Note what neither direction can show: whether the runtime keeps one first-declaration map or two with a cross-kind lookup — those are indistinguishable from source, so no description here claims it. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
